abstract: NMR structures are deposited as ensembles of conformers, and their precision is reported after superposition on a chosen set of residues, a choice that is difficult for proteins with several domains or flexible regions. We present RESUPER, a program that identifies rigid domains, selects a superposition range for each domain, and detects distinct conformational states in protein ensembles. RESUPER follows the two-stage method of CYRANGE, but each domain split is decided by a geometric test that can be checked on the structure. On two test sets fixed before evaluation, RESUPER counted the domains correctly in 95 of 96 and 45 of 48 ensembles (CYRANGE: 76 and 39) and put two separate rigid bodies into one range in 0 and 4 ensembles (CYRANGE: 17 and 9). On 222 randomly selected NMR entries, the two programs gave the same number of domains for 88% of the entries, and none of four prespecified comparisons, applied post hoc to CYRANGE, showed a statistically significant difference. For apo-Pin1 (PDB 7SA5), RESUPER found the two deposited conformational states. Analyzed separately, one state has a single superposition range covering both domains and the other has separate ranges. RESUPER is integrated into POKY with a graphical user interface.
